newsitem.title: USA: Illinois jobless rate falls to five pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Illinois jobless rate falls to five pct in January.

text.p: Illinois' unemployment rate fell to a seasonally adjusted five percent in January from 5.2 percent in December, the state's Department of Employment Security reported Tuesday.

"Illinois is striding a healthy economic course marked by strong employment, consistently low unemployment and steady job growths, and all of these indicators have remained at a near constant level for more than a year," Lynn Doherty, the department's director, said in a news release.

The state reported that 305,968 people were unemployed last month, compared to 320,059 jobless workers in December. Illinois' January 1996 unemployment rate was 5.3 percent with 324,687 workers without jobs.
The number of employed workers grew to a record 5.82 million in January from 5.80 million in December, according to the department.
